name: citation: an answer that covers everything except the allergy
input: This is acute primary angle closure in the right eye, and the left eye has a narrow angle so it is at risk too. It was probably set off by the dark cinema and the chlorphenamine she has just started, so I would stop the chlorphenamine. I would lie her flat and give analgesia and an antiemetic. To lower the pressure I would give timolol and apraclonidine drops, intravenous acetazolamide, and pilocarpine once the pressure starts to fall. When the cornea has cleared she needs laser peripheral iridotomy to both eyes, including the fellow eye. After the attack settles I would repeat gonioscopy of the right eye and look at both optic discs.
expected: Gap chosen: "Note the sulfonamide allergy before giving acetazolamide". The passage on pp. 5–6 is retrieved. Cited sentence (p. 6): "Check for sulfonamide allergy, kidney disease, low potassium and sickle cell disease before giving it.". Support check: supported.
observed: Gap chosen: "Note the sulfonamide allergy before giving acetazolamide". Revision point: "Check for sulfonamide allergy before giving acetazolamide.". Cited p. 6: "Check for sulfonamide allergy, kidney disease, low potassium and sickle cell disease before giving it.". Support check: supported.

cited.excerpt: Check for sulfonamide allergy, kidney disease, low potassium and sickle cell disease before giving it.
cited.heading: Managing an acute attack › Immediate treatment — Systemic carbonic anhydrase inhibitor.
